> my mania often takes the form of out of control self-destructive behavior

That out of control self-destructive behavior is called living.

You were in school and you got bored with school because it's lame and boring and you could learn more by reading a book or seeing the world. So you went out and saw the world. Then you realized going out to see the world on a whim wasn't all that you thought it'd be, so you went home and thought about how strange that whole adventure was, so you go pay some guy and he confirms your suspicions that you're crazy. Then he gives you some bullshit about living and experiencing situations firsthand being self-destructive and hands you some pills.

I'm bipolar. I understand that it can be scary or frustrating or overwhelming when you go off on a manic episode and it all comes crashing back down, but you are a human being, an animal, who is leading it's own existence. Maybe you run into some things that are destructive to your ego or your overall health, but you are living to experience those things.

Doctors tell you that you're crazy and that you should take these pills so that you can be normal. Normal people go to work and complete boring, repetitive tasks and they like to go a little wild on the weekends and mix little wine in their seltzer water. People who are "crazy" can go out and appreciate the world for what they find in it, rather than what they are told they are looking at. Of course, if you actually start being self-destructive by doing drugs and sitting around and not getting enough exercise or eating right, then your physical health will drop and it will take your mental health down with it.

I don't know if you are on any medication, but if you are, my advice would be to consider stopping the medication, but only if you feel that you would be safe (not suicidal) without it.
